pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Reported revenue growth overstates underlying momentum: acquisitions, including Antares Vision, supplied most of the latest reported increase while DTT organic sales declined. DTT’s Q3 margin is below the former CPI-only perimeter, but segment reorganization and acquired-intangible amortization make this comparison non-like-for-like. Integration remains a near-term cash-flow test rather than a proven source of deleveraging. Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15

Positive free cash flow supports debt service, but does not yet demonstrate a reduction in creditor risk: carrying-value net debt increased and reported LTM leverage is higher than at FY2025. The issuer’s lower adjusted leverage uses a different debt and EBITDA definition, so the two ratios should not be blended. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

Customer concentration is material within SAT: one unnamed customer accounted for a substantial share of sales, leaving that segment exposed to customer order, renewal and product decisions that cannot be monitored through named-customer disclosures. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation C2-05

runs.text: The principal strengths are demonstrated post-capex cash generation, a larger backlog, SAT’s current profit contribution and debt facilities with stated maturities several years beyond the latest reporting date. Each provides time or cash-flow capacity to service debt if backlog converts and acquired activities improve. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

The principal weaknesses are the increase in carrying-value net debt, the acquisition-related operating loss and lower DTT margin, persistent SAT customer concentration, and incomplete loan maturity allocation. Together they reduce visibility into the pace of deleveraging, concentration resilience and the amount of debt requiring refinancing at each stated date. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15, 20–21

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Crane NXT acquired OpSec Security in May 2024 for a base purchase price of USD 270.0 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis; net cash paid was USD 268.4 million, funded with USD 210.0 million from the revolving facility and cash on hand. De La Rue Authentication Solutions was acquired in May 2025 at a base price of GBP 300.0 million, cash-free and debt-free; the filing reports final net cash paid of USD 391.1 million and use of Term Loan A. The sources do not provide transaction-level pro forma leverage or a purchase multiple for either acquisition. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84

Crane NXT began its multi-phase Antares Vision acquisition in December 2025, paying EUR 117.3 million, approximately USD 137.8 million, for an initial 32.3% interest. The remaining shares were acquired through the tender and squeeze-out completed in March 2026 for EUR 244.2 million, approximately USD 281.9 million; the filing reports total consideration of USD 416.9 million. Antares provides inspection, detection and track-and-trace systems for life-sciences and food-and-beverage customers. Its post-acquisition contribution included operating losses attributed by the issuer to acquisition-related amortization and transaction costs, so standalone cash returns are not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10, 13

The Fifth Amendment in December 2025 established a EUR 430 million senior secured delayed-draw Term Loan B due in December 2032, extended the existing Term Loan A and revolving facility maturities to December 2030, and increased the revolving commitment to USD 800.0 million. A July 2026 repricing increased the Term Loan B to EUR 480 million; the incremental EUR 50 million and cash on hand were used primarily to repay Term Loan A. The Q3 filing also reports borrowings and repayments used to fund Antares, repay assumed Antares debt and support working capital. The executed amendment texts are not included in the pinned sources, limiting conclusions about covenant capacity and collateral terms. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.value: Crane NXT’s secure-payment and authentication activities have identifiable customer uses and disclosed order backlog, but a significant SAT customer, recent acquisitions and a reorganized operating structure make revenue concentration, segment comparability and acquired-business returns material creditor questions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating model spans payment-verification equipment and software, field services, banknotes, product security and authentication. FY2025 sales were nearly balanced between CPI and SAT, but the segment structure changed after Antares Vision was acquired and CPI was combined with Antares in DTT. Annual and current segment figures therefore do not form a like-for-like time series.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - A persistent customer concentration is disclosed within SAT: one individually significant customer generated USD 210.7 million of FY2025 sales, after USD 209.2 million in FY2024 and USD 213.1 million in FY2023. The FY2025 amount equaled 26.0% of SAT and 12.7% of total company sales, exposing results to customer-specific order and renewal decisions even though the customer is not named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisition risk is material to current operating analysis: Antares Vision contributed sales while reporting an operating loss during 2026, and DTT’s reported quarterly operating profit and margin were below the prior-year quarter even as acquired sales lifted the segment’s total. The issuer attributes Antares’s operating loss to acquisition-related amortization and transaction costs, but standalone cash returns remain unestablished.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership evidence establishes public listing and acquired operating assets, but does not identify current beneficial shareholders, their economic stakes or shareholder-level control rights. The public-company evidence cannot support a sponsor-alignment conclusion; the detailed ownership view remains insufficiently established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisition funding and ordinary dividends are disclosed, but the pinned documents do not provide purchase multiples, transaction-level pro forma leverage or enough legal detail to assess acquisition returns and capacity. The evidence supports monitoring cash retention and integration outcomes, not a conclusion that shareholder extraction occurred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest counterweight is that FY2025 sales were distributed across two substantial product segments and the year-end order book was expected to convert predominantly in the following fiscal year; the latest release also showed a larger total backlog, including acquired Antares orders. SAT reported stronger year-over-year quarterly profit, and management said it delivered synergy commitments and remained on track for its year-end deleveraging objective. These points support demand visibility and potential acquisition benefits, but management’s statements do not establish realized cash savings or acquisition returns. The view would improve with sustained organic growth, stable segment margins after the reorganization, reported Antares cash generation and debt paydown, and disclosure of the shareholder and legal-control structure; it would weaken if acquired-business losses persist, backlog conversion slips, or further borrowing funds acquisitions or distributions without commensurate cash generation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The conclusion on shareholder influence and governance remains limited because the supplied filings do not identify current beneficial owners, ownership percentages or investor-specific voting arrangements; the current proxy and related governance documents are needed to establish whether ownership is concentrated.

fields.value: - FY2025 control conclusions do not cover DLR’s internal-control systems, which were excluded from the company’s control assessment as a recently acquired business; this reduces assurance over the acquired operation’s processes until integration is completed.

fields.value: Crane NXT began its multi-phase Antares Vision acquisition in December 2025, paying EUR 117.3 million, approximately USD 137.8 million, for an initial 32.3% interest. The remaining shares were acquired through the tender and squeeze-out completed in March 2026 for EUR 244.2 million, approximately USD 281.9 million; the filing reports total consideration of USD 416.9 million. Antares provides inspection, detection and track-and-trace systems for life-sciences and food-and-beverage customers. Its post-acquisition contribution included operating losses attributed by the issuer to acquisition-related amortization and transaction costs, so standalone cash returns are not established.

A July 2026 repricing increased the Term Loan B to EUR 480 million; the incremental EUR 50 million and cash on hand were used primarily to repay Term Loan A. The Q3 filing also reports borrowings and repayments used to fund Antares, repay assumed Antares debt and support working capital. The executed amendment texts are not included in the pinned sources, limiting conclusions about covenant capacity and collateral terms.

Integration remains a near-term cash-flow test rather than a proven source of deleveraging.

fields.value: The strongest counterweight is cash generation alongside higher reported order backlog. The latest release also gives FY2026 sales-growth and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance, though this remains management’s forward-looking view rather than a realized result. Those indicators could support faster deleveraging if backlog converts, acquired businesses move toward operating profitability and cash is retained for debt reduction. The view would improve with successive periods of organic growth, DTT margin recovery and lower carrying net debt; it would weaken if acquired sales mask continued organic contraction, Antares operating losses persist or distributions and further acquisitions consume cash generation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Crane NXT combines authentication, payment-verification, product-security and traceability activities, with cash generation that has covered capital spending and cash interest in the latest reported period. The creditor case is constrained by a sharp increase in carrying debt following acquisitions, carrying-value leverage above the issuer-adjusted presentation, SAT customer concentration and the acquired Antares business’s operating loss. A larger backlog and positive free cash flow provide support, but backlog is not cash and the segment reorganization limits annual comparability. The primary downside path is delayed integration or customer/order weakness reducing margins and cash conversion, slowing debt reduction and increasing dependence on future refinancing. Stated loan maturities are several years away, although principal allocations by maturity are incomplete.

fields.value: The following metrics show improving current-period cash generation alongside higher leverage and acquisition-related operating volatility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Crane NXT sells equipment, software and services used to verify currency and payments, protect physical products, and authenticate or trace products through supply chains. SAT’s banknote and product-security activity provides a current profit offset to DTT; DTT combines the former CPI business with Antares Vision. This addition broadens the product and end-market set but creates integration risk and makes pre- and post-acquisition segment comparisons non-like-for-like. The filings identify a persistent individually significant SAT customer, but do not name it or disclose its contract duration. Those facts constrain conclusions about customer switching costs and renewal resilience.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The source evidence supports a limited competitive assessment: proprietary authentication solutions and customer use in banknotes, consumer goods and government tax stamps create differentiated product applications, while the significant SAT customer and lower DTT organic sales demonstrate concentrated demand and exposure to order timing. The documents do not quantify market share, switching costs, supplier dependence or competitor pricing, so those factors do not support a stronger competitive-position conclusion. The annual report identifies macroeconomic, trade-policy, inflation, foreign-exchange and geopolitical risks that could weaken customer demand, raise sourcing costs or make refinancing less favorable. It also reports FY2025 interest-rate and currency sensitivities, but neither those disclosures nor the subsequent interim filing quantify current demand, input-cost or refinancing sensitivities. In credit-translated SWOT terms, backlog and SAT profitability are supports; acquired-business losses, customer concentration, rising debt and non-comparable segment history are constraints; Antares’s life-science and food traceability applications are a potential growth avenue, while delayed integration or order conversion is the principal threat.

The improvement supports debt service, but cash flow was not fully available for principal reduction: acquisition payments and dividends competed with deleveraging, and the Antares contribution has not been separately reconciled to post-close EBITDA and cash generation. Reported LTM cash-interest cover remains positive, but carrying-value net debt and leverage increased since year-end. The company’s 2.5x figure uses adjusted EBITDA and principal before financing costs; it is not directly comparable with the 3.03x carrying-value net leverage calculation.

fields.value: The Credit Agreement facilities have stated maturities several years beyond the latest reporting date. The latest filing does not allocate all current loan principal by maturity year, so the stated dates identify refinancing windows but not a complete maturity wall. A revolving commitment is disclosed, but current letter-of-credit use is not reported; the FY2025 filing reported USD 97.5 million of standby letters, so current undrawn liquidity cannot be inferred from that older balance. This leaves the near-term liquidity conclusion supported by positive cash and operating cash flow, while exact committed availability and facility headroom remain unestablished.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next year, the main upside is conversion of the reported backlog and realization of management’s stated FY2026 sales-growth and adjusted-margin outlook. Over a longer horizon, Antares may expand traceability exposure in life sciences and food and beverage, but the filings do not establish standalone acquired-business returns. The principal downside is a delayed integration or weaker customer and order demand: DTT’s acquired contribution would fail to cover its lower organic sales, group operating profit would weaken, and working-capital absorption could reduce free cash flow. Lower cash generation would slow debt reduction and increase reliance on refinancing, although stated facility maturities are not immediate. Cost alignment and cash retention are management levers, but the supplied evidence does not quantify savings, fixed-cost flexibility or downside runway.

The business cannot be ranked against typical leveraged-credit issuers from these issuer-only materials. Financial capacity weakened on a carrying-value basis since FY2025, although positive cash flow moderates the pressure. Refinancing depends on organic demand, acquired-margin repair, cash retention and execution ahead of stated facility dates; the principal downside is weaker orders or delayed integration reducing margins and cash conversion. A more definitive view needs a current loan-principal schedule by maturity and an integrated cash forecast that tests customer, margin and working-capital shocks.
